title: Sea Bass, Chilean, Frozen, Wild Caught

content.title: About
content.content: Sea bass (family Serranidae) is a marine fish native to the Pacific coast of Chile. Wild‑caught and quickly frozen after harvest, it retains its fresh flavor, firm texture, and nutritional value.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chilean sea bass is prized for its delicate taste and buttery flesh.
Wild individuals feed on small fish and crustaceans, which enriches the meat with omega‑3 fatty acids.
Quick‑freeze (IQF) technology preserves up to 90 % of vitamins and minerals.
Adults can reach up to 70 cm and over 4 kg, but commercial portions usually come from smaller specimens.
Chile regulates wild sea bass fisheries with quotas to prevent over‑exploitation.

items.title: Rich in omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Omega‑3s support heart health, reduce inflammation, and promote brain function.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: A 100‑g serving provides about 20 g of complete protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Source of vitamin D
items.content: Vitamin D aids calcium absorption and supports the immune system.

items.title: Minerals: selenium and iodine
items.content: Selenium acts as an antioxidant, while iodine is vital for thyroid function.

items.title: Low mercury levels
items.content: Wild sea bass from cold waters typically contains less mercury than larger predatory fish.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to marine fish, including sea bass.

items.title: Sodium in processing
items.content: Industrial freezing may involve a light brine; check the label if you need to limit sodium intake.

items.title: Food‑borne risk if mishandled
items.content: If thawed above 4 °C for more than 2 hours, bacterial growth can occur.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Sea bass can be baked, pan‑seared, steamed, or used in sushi and sashimi after full thawing. Avoid overcooking to keep the flesh tender and moist.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the frozen product at –18 °C or lower. Once thawed, use within 1–2 days and store in a sealed container in the refrigerator at 0–4 °C.
